findings.where: First screen, the portrait filling the right of the frame (desktop), and the inset portrait on phone
findings.fault: The portrait's backdrop is still a cool, slightly green-grey. Across about 40% of the first screen it sits beside the warm ivory paper and the pale yellow address strip, so the screen shows three grounds instead of one soft paper ground. The palette note says the photographs are multiplied onto the paper so that their light backdrops take its warmth, but the render does not show that. The grey reads as a cold panel set into the sheet, not as Mark standing in the paper's light.
findings.who_objects: The founder judges the first screen first. The brief asks for one soft ground and imagery graded into the house colours. A visitor sees a photo pasted onto a document rather than a single sheet, which weakens the 'counsel's paper' idea at the moment it should land.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lectern photograph under the opening paragraphs (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The greyscale treatment turns the purple stage backdrop into a flat charcoal close to the logo grey. This makes it the largest and darkest area on the whole page, a heavy slab on the quiet ivory text column. The hero shows Mark in colour, while the article shows him in grey against near-black, so the two photos of him are treated differently.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for 'alive, not boring' and a calm ground. Someone at a development bank reading an article meets a dark block that is heavier than anything else on the page and a grey, flat Mark, unlike the warm man on the homepage.

findings.where: First screen frame: the portrait on desktop against the portrait on phone
findings.fault: On desktop the portrait runs flush to the hairline frame's top, right and bottom edges, as the texture note says ('the portrait set flush against it'). On phone it floats inset inside the frame with margins on all sides, while the yellow strip below it still runs flush to the frame. One surface gets two treatments, and the stated rule holds only at desktop.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, or whoever builds the real page, gets two contradictory rules for how a photo meets the document edge. A phone visitor sees a boxed photo inside a boxed sheet, which looks fussier than the desktop page.

findings.fault: The curve is drawn in the house blue, which the palette gives only to the wordmark, links and focus. That makes it the one non-link use of blue on the page, beside a blue underlined 'Replay the entrance' link.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reads the palette's role table against the tile. The brief for this direction says 'blue only on the wordmark and links'. A visitor may read the blue line as something to click.
